overall: The AG found one violation: the Board failed to keep its website-as-official-posting-location notice conspicuously visible at Town Hall entrances because a holiday wreath obstructed it. Other allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not post notice of its January 13 meeting at least 48 hours in advance.
allegations.key_passage: First, we find that the Board posted notice for its January 13 meeting to the Town’s website, which is the official notice posting location, more than 48 hours in advance of the meeting, and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 13 meeting notice did not contain the date and time it was posted.
Complainant alleged the notice describing the Town's website as its official posting location was not properly posted at Town Hall entrances.
allegations.key_passage: Here, where the notice was not visible to the public at all hours at both the main and handicapped accessible entrance because it was obstructed by a wreath during the holiday season, we find the Board did not comply with this requirement.

allegations.summary: Complainant noted the meeting packet was not posted 48 hours before the January 13 meeting, which the letter treats as a possible additional allegation.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that meeting packets be posted or provided to the public in advance of a meeting; therefore, even if true, this allegation does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
